343:     public override void Initialize(AnalysisContext context)
344:     {
345:         context.EnableConcurrentExecution();
346:         context.ConfigureGeneratedCodeAnalysis(GeneratedCodeAnalysisFlags.Analyze | GeneratedCodeAnalysisFlags.ReportDiagnostics);
347:         context.RegisterCompilationStartAction(context =>
348:         {
349:             if (ReferenceSymbols.TryCreate(context.Compilation, out ReferenceSymbols? typeReferences))
350:             {
351:                 // Search the compilation for implementations of IMessagePackFormatter<T>.
352:                 ImmutableHashSet<FormatterDescriptor> formatterTypes = this.SearchForFormatters(context.Compilation.Assembly.GlobalNamespace).ToImmutableHashSet();
353: 
354:                 AnalyzerOptions options = new AnalyzerOptions()
355:                     .WithFormatterTypes(ImmutableArray<FormattableType>.Empty, formatterTypes)
356:                     .WithAssemblyAttributes(context.Compilation.Assembly.GetAttributes(), context.CancellationToken);
357:                 context.RegisterSymbolAction(context => this.AnalyzeSymbol(context, typeReferences, options), SymbolKind.NamedType);
358:                 context.RegisterSymbolStartAction(context => SymbolStartAction(context, typeReferences, options), SymbolKind.NamedType);
359:             }
360:         });
361:     }
362: 
363:     private static void SymbolStartAction(SymbolStartAnalysisContext context, ReferenceSymbols typeReferences, AnalyzerOptions options)
364:     {
365:         INamedTypeSymbol declaredSymbol = (INamedTypeSymbol)context.Symbol;
366:         QualifiedNamedTypeName typeName = new(declaredSymbol);
367: 
368:         // If this is a formatter, confirm that it meets requirements.
369:         if (options.KnownFormattersByName.TryGetValue(typeName, out FormatterDescriptor? formatter))
370:         {
371:             // Call out any formattable reference types that are not nullable.
372:             INamedTypeSymbol[] missing = (
373:                 from iface in declaredSymbol.Interfaces
374:                 where SymbolEqualityComparer.Default.Equals(iface.ConstructUnboundGenericType(), typeReferences.MessagePackFormatterOfT) &&
375:                     iface.TypeArguments is [INamedTypeSymbol { IsReferenceType: true, NullableAnnotation: NullableAnnotation.NotAnnotated } a]
376:                 select (INamedTypeSymbol)iface.TypeArguments[0]).ToArray();
377: 
378:             if (missing.Length > 0)
379:             {
380:                 // Look for the base list so we can report the diagnostic(s) at the actual type argument.
381:                 context.RegisterSyntaxNodeAction(
382:                     context =>
383:                     {
384:                         BaseListSyntax baseList = (BaseListSyntax)context.Node;
385: 
386:                         // Find the location of the actual generic type argument if we can.
387:                         foreach (BaseTypeSyntax baseTypeSyntax in baseList.Types)
388:                         {
389:                             if (baseTypeSyntax.Type is GenericNameSyntax { TypeArgumentList: { Arguments: [TypeSyntax typeArg] } })
390:                             {
391:                                 ITypeSymbol? actual = context.SemanticModel.GetTypeInfo(typeArg, context.CancellationToken).Type;
392:                                 if (missing.Any(m => SymbolEqualityComparer.Default.Equals(actual, m)))
393:                                 {
394:                                     Location location = typeArg.GetLocation();
395:                                     context.ReportDiagnostic(Diagnostic.Create(NullableReferenceTypeFormatter, location, typeArg.ToString()));
396:                                     break;
397:                                 }
398:                             }
399:                         }
400:                     },
401:                     SyntaxKind.BaseList);
402:             }
403:         }
404:     }
405: 
406:     private void AnalyzeSymbol(SymbolAnalysisContext context, ReferenceSymbols typeReferences, AnalyzerOptions options)
407:     {
408:         INamedTypeSymbol declaredSymbol = (INamedTypeSymbol)context.Symbol;
409:         QualifiedNamedTypeName typeName = new(declaredSymbol);
410: 
411:         // If this is a formatter, confirm that it meets requirements.
412:         if (options.KnownFormattersByName.TryGetValue(typeName, out FormatterDescriptor? formatter))
413:         {
414:             // Look for colliding formatters (multiple formatters that want to format the same type).
415:             foreach (FormattableType formattableType in options.GetCollidingFormatterDataTypes(typeName))
416:             {
417:                 context.ReportDiagnostic(Diagnostic.Create(CollidingFormatters, declaredSymbol.Locations[0], formattableType.Name.GetQualifiedName(Qualifiers.Namespace)));
418:             }
419: 
420:             if (!formatter.ExcludeFromSourceGeneratedResolver && formatter.InaccessibleDescriptor is { } inaccessible)
421:             {
422:                 context.ReportDiagnostic(Diagnostic.Create(inaccessible, declaredSymbol.Locations[0]));
423:             }
424:         }
425: 
426:         switch (declaredSymbol.TypeKind)
427:         {
428:             case TypeKind.Interface when declaredSymbol.GetAttributes().Any(x2 => SymbolEqualityComparer.Default.Equals(x2.AttributeClass, typeReferences.UnionAttribute)):
429:             case TypeKind.Class or TypeKind.Struct when declaredSymbol.GetAttributes().Any(x2 => SymbolEqualityComparer.Default.Equals(x2.AttributeClass, typeReferences.MessagePackObjectAttribute)):
430:                 TypeCollector.Collect(context.Compilation, options, typeReferences, context.ReportDiagnostic, declaredSymbol, context.CancellationToken);
431:                 break;
432:         }
433:     }
434: 
435:     private IEnumerable<FormatterDescriptor> SearchForFormatters(INamespaceOrTypeSymbol container)
436:     {
437:         if (container is INamespaceSymbol ns)
438:         {
439:             foreach (INamespaceSymbol childNamespace in ns.GetNamespaceMembers())
440:             {
441:                 foreach (FormatterDescriptor x in this.SearchForFormatters(childNamespace))
442:                 {
443:                     yield return x;
444:                 }
445:             }
446:         }
447: 
448:         foreach (INamedTypeSymbol type in container.GetTypeMembers())
449:         {
450:             if (type.DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault()?.SyntaxTree.FilePath.Contains("MessagePack.SourceGenerator") is true)
451:             {
452:                 // We do not want to find source generated formatters during analysis.
453:                 continue;
454:             }
455: 
456:             if (FormatterDescriptor.TryCreate(type, out FormatterDescriptor? formatter))
457:             {
458:                 yield return formatter;
459:             }
460: 
461:             foreach (FormatterDescriptor nested in this.SearchForFormatters(type))
462:             {
463:                 yield return nested;
464:             }
465:         }
466:     }
467: }

1: # Contributing
2: 
3: ## Dependencies
4: 
5: * [Visual Studio 2022](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/)
6: * [Unity Editor](https://unity3d.com/unity/editor) (optional)
7: * .NET Core SDK and runtimes (run `init` to install)
8: 
9: This repo uses the .NET Core SDK and runtimes to build and test the projects.
10: You can install the right versions of the SDK and runtimes by running the `init.ps1` script at the root of the repo.
11: 
12: By default no elevation is required as these toolsets are installed in a per-user directory. Launching `devenv` from the same PowerShell window that you ran the script will lead VS to discover these per-user toolsets.
13: To get VS to find the toolsets when launched from the Start Menu, run `init -InstallLocality machine`, which requires elevation for each SDK or runtime installed.
14: 
15: ## How to Build
16: 
17: Open `MessagePack.sln` on Visual Studio 2022.
18: 
19: Alternatively you may build from the command line using `msbuild.exe` or:
20: 
21:     dotnet build /p:platform=NoVSIX
22: 
23: ## Unity
24: 
25: See the ReadMe for the target directory `src\MessagePack.UnityClient` for information on building and managing with Unity. Unity's CI is managed in `unity.yml` in GitHub Actions.
26: 
27: ## How to Publish Package
28: 
29: Package publishing is triggered via GitHub Actions using workflow_dispatch. Follow these steps:
30: 
31: 1. Select Actions -> "Run release build and publish to NuGet"
32: 2. Enter a version tag (e.g., `v3.0.1`)
33: 3. Click "Run workflow"
34: 
35: ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/74886c88-f6d1-4108-8ce1-02d3d1b31f1f)
36: 
37: The workflow will:
38: - Update the version in [MessagePack.UnityClient/Assets/Scripts/MessagePack/package.json](https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/blob/master/src/MessagePack.UnityClient/Assets/Scripts/MessagePack/package.json)
39: - Commit and push the change
40: - Build the .NET library
41: - Publish to [NuGet/MessagePack](https://www.nuget.org/packages/MessagePack)
42: - Create a draft GitHub release
43: 
44: After CI completion, edit the release draft to add relevant release notes and announcements.
45: 
46: ### Secret
47: 
48: The following secrets are managed at the organization level:
49: 
50: * `UNITY_EMAIL`
51: * `UNITY_LICENSE`
52: * `UNITY_PASSWORD`
53: * `NUGET_KEY`
54: 
55: The `UNITY_*` secrets are personal license keys required for Unity builds.
56: 
57: `NUGET_KEY` is a key required for releasing nupkg files, and since it has a 365-day expiration period, the key needs to be regenerated when it expires.

343:     public override void Initialize(AnalysisContext context)
344:     {
345:         context.EnableConcurrentExecution();
346:         context.ConfigureGeneratedCodeAnalysis(GeneratedCodeAnalysisFlags.Analyze | GeneratedCodeAnalysisFlags.ReportDiagnostics);
347:         context.RegisterCompilationStartAction(context =>
348:         {
349:             if (ReferenceSymbols.TryCreate(context.Compilation, out ReferenceSymbols? typeReferences))
350:             {
351:                 // Search the compilation for implementations of IMessagePackFormatter<T>.
352:                 ImmutableHashSet<FormatterDescriptor> formatterTypes = this.SearchForFormatters(context.Compilation.Assembly.GlobalNamespace).ToImmutableHashSet();
353: 
354:                 AnalyzerOptions options = new AnalyzerOptions()
355:                     .WithFormatterTypes(ImmutableArray<FormattableType>.Empty, formatterTypes)
356:                     .WithAssemblyAttributes(context.Compilation.Assembly.GetAttributes(), context.CancellationToken);
357:                 context.RegisterSymbolAction(context => this.AnalyzeSymbol(context, typeReferences, options), SymbolKind.NamedType);
358:                 context.RegisterSymbolStartAction(context => SymbolStartAction(context, typeReferences, options), SymbolKind.NamedType);
359:             }
360:         });
361:     }
362: 
363:     private static void SymbolStartAction(SymbolStartAnalysisContext context, ReferenceSymbols typeReferences, AnalyzerOptions options)
364:     {
365:         INamedTypeSymbol declaredSymbol = (INamedTypeSymbol)context.Symbol;
366:         QualifiedNamedTypeName typeName = new(declaredSymbol);
367: 
368:         // If this is a formatter, confirm that it meets requirements.
369:         if (options.KnownFormattersByName.TryGetValue(typeName, out FormatterDescriptor? formatter))
370:         {
371:             // Call out any formattable reference types that are not nullable.
372:             INamedTypeSymbol[] missing = (
373:                 from iface in declaredSymbol.Interfaces
374:                 where SymbolEqualityComparer.Default.Equals(iface.ConstructUnboundGenericType(), typeReferences.MessagePackFormatterOfT) &&
375:                     iface.TypeArguments is [INamedTypeSymbol { IsReferenceType: true, NullableAnnotation: NullableAnnotation.NotAnnotated } a]
376:                 select (INamedTypeSymbol)iface.TypeArguments[0]).ToArray();
377: 
378:             if (missing.Length > 0)
379:             {
380:                 // Look for the base list so we can report the diagnostic(s) at the actual type argument.
381:                 context.RegisterSyntaxNodeAction(
382:                     context =>
383:                     {
384:                         BaseListSyntax baseList = (BaseListSyntax)context.Node;
385: 
386:                         // Find the location of the actual generic type argument if we can.
387:                         foreach (BaseTypeSyntax baseTypeSyntax in baseList.Types)
388:                         {
389:                             if (baseTypeSyntax.Type is GenericNameSyntax { TypeArgumentList: { Arguments: [TypeSyntax typeArg] } })
390:                             {
391:                                 ITypeSymbol? actual = context.SemanticModel.GetTypeInfo(typeArg, context.CancellationToken).Type;
392:                                 if (missing.Any(m => SymbolEqualityComparer.Default.Equals(actual, m)))
393:                                 {
394:                                     Location location = typeArg.GetLocation();
395:                                     context.ReportDiagnostic(Diagnostic.Create(NullableReferenceTypeFormatter, location, typeArg.ToString()));
396:                                     break;
397:                                 }
398:                             }
399:                         }
400:                     },
401:                     SyntaxKind.BaseList);
402:             }
403:         }
404:     }
405: 
406:     private void AnalyzeSymbol(SymbolAnalysisContext context, ReferenceSymbols typeReferences, AnalyzerOptions options)
407:     {
408:         INamedTypeSymbol declaredSymbol = (INamedTypeSymbol)context.Symbol;
409:         QualifiedNamedTypeName typeName = new(declaredSymbol);
410: 
411:         // If this is a formatter, confirm that it meets requirements.
412:         if (options.KnownFormattersByName.TryGetValue(typeName, out FormatterDescriptor? formatter))
413:         {
414:             // Look for colliding formatters (multiple formatters that want to format the same type).
415:             foreach (FormattableType formattableType in options.GetCollidingFormatterDataTypes(typeName))
416:             {
417:                 context.ReportDiagnostic(Diagnostic.Create(CollidingFormatters, declaredSymbol.Locations[0], formattableType.Name.GetQualifiedName(Qualifiers.Namespace)));
418:             }
419: 
420:             if (!formatter.ExcludeFromSourceGeneratedResolver && formatter.InaccessibleDescriptor is { } inaccessible)
421:             {
422:                 context.ReportDiagnostic(Diagnostic.Create(inaccessible, declaredSymbol.Locations[0]));
423:             }
424:         }
425: 
426:         switch (declaredSymbol.TypeKind)
427:         {
428:             case TypeKind.Interface when declaredSymbol.GetAttributes().Any(x2 => SymbolEqualityComparer.Default.Equals(x2.AttributeClass, typeReferences.UnionAttribute)):
429:             case TypeKind.Class or TypeKind.Struct when declaredSymbol.GetAttributes().Any(x2 => SymbolEqualityComparer.Default.Equals(x2.AttributeClass, typeReferences.MessagePackObjectAttribute)):
430:                 TypeCollector.Collect(context.Compilation, options, typeReferences, context.ReportDiagnostic, declaredSymbol, context.CancellationToken);
431:                 break;
432:         }
433:     }
434: 
435:     private IEnumerable<FormatterDescriptor> SearchForFormatters(INamespaceOrTypeSymbol container)
436:     {
437:         if (container is INamespaceSymbol ns)
438:         {
439:             foreach (INamespaceSymbol childNamespace in ns.GetNamespaceMembers())
440:             {
441:                 foreach (FormatterDescriptor x in this.SearchForFormatters(childNamespace))
442:                 {
443:                     yield return x;
444:                 }
445:             }
446:         }
447: 
448:         foreach (INamedTypeSymbol type in container.GetTypeMembers())
449:         {
450:             if (type.DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault()?.SyntaxTree.FilePath.Contains("MessagePack.SourceGenerator") is true)
451:             {
452:                 // We do not want to find source generated formatters during analysis.
453:                 continue;
454:             }
455: 
456:             if (FormatterDescriptor.TryCreate(type, out FormatterDescriptor? formatter))
457:             {
458:                 yield return formatter;
459:             }
460: 
461:             foreach (FormatterDescriptor nested in this.SearchForFormatters(type))
462:             {
463:                 yield return nested;
464:             }
465:         }
466:     }
467: }

1: # Contributing
2: 
3: ## Dependencies
4: 
5: * [Visual Studio 2022](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/)
6: * [Unity Editor](https://unity3d.com/unity/editor) (optional)
7: * .NET Core SDK and runtimes (run `init` to install)
8: 
9: This repo uses the .NET Core SDK and runtimes to build and test the projects.
10: You can install the right versions of the SDK and runtimes by running the `init.ps1` script at the root of the repo.
11: 
12: By default no elevation is required as these toolsets are installed in a per-user directory. Launching `devenv` from the same PowerShell window that you ran the script will lead VS to discover these per-user toolsets.
13: To get VS to find the toolsets when launched from the Start Menu, run `init -InstallLocality machine`, which requires elevation for each SDK or runtime installed.
14: 
15: ## How to Build
16: 
17: Open `MessagePack.sln` on Visual Studio 2022.
18: 
19: Alternatively you may build from the command line using `msbuild.exe` or:
20: 
21:     dotnet build /p:platform=NoVSIX
22: 
23: ## Unity
24: 
25: See the ReadMe for the target directory `src\MessagePack.UnityClient` for information on building and managing with Unity. Unity's CI is managed in `unity.yml` in GitHub Actions.
26: 
27: ## How to Publish Package
28: 
29: Package publishing is triggered via GitHub Actions using workflow_dispatch. Follow these steps:
30: 
31: 1. Select Actions -> "Run release build and publish to NuGet"
32: 2. Enter a version tag (e.g., `v3.0.1`)
33: 3. Click "Run workflow"
34: 
35: ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/74886c88-f6d1-4108-8ce1-02d3d1b31f1f)
36: 
37: The workflow will:
38: - Update the version in [MessagePack.UnityClient/Assets/Scripts/MessagePack/package.json](https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/blob/master/src/MessagePack.UnityClient/Assets/Scripts/MessagePack/package.json)
39: - Commit and push the change
40: - Build the .NET library
41: - Publish to [NuGet/MessagePack](https://www.nuget.org/packages/MessagePack)
42: - Create a draft GitHub release
43: 
44: After CI completion, edit the release draft to add relevant release notes and announcements.
45: 
46: ### Secret
47: 
48: The following secrets are managed at the organization level:
49: 
50: * `UNITY_EMAIL`
51: * `UNITY_LICENSE`
52: * `UNITY_PASSWORD`
53: * `NUGET_KEY`
54: 
55: The `UNITY_*` secrets are personal license keys required for Unity builds.
56: 
57: `NUGET_KEY` is a key required for releasing nupkg files, and since it has a 365-day expiration period, the key needs to be regenerated when it expires.
